blocks.title: Después de este pdf sabrás
bullets: usar la inversión después de palabras negativas o restrictivas (Never have I seen ...)
hacer condicionales sin if (Had I known ...)
dar énfasis con oraciones escindidas (What I need is ...)
usar do / does / did para dar énfasis

blocks.text: 1. La inversión después de palabras negativas
En inglés formal y literario se puede empezar una frase con una palabra negativa o restrictiva. Entonces va el orden de pregunta: el verbo auxiliar delante del sujeto.

head: Inicio
Ejemplo
Español
rows: Never
Never have I seen such a mess.
Nunca había visto semejante desorden.
Rarely / Seldom
Rarely do we get such good weather.
Pocas veces tenemos tan buen tiempo.
Not only ... but also
Not only is it cheap, but it's also fast.
No solo es barato, sino que además es rápido.
Hardly ... when
Hardly had I arrived when it started to rain.
Apenas había llegado cuando empezó a llover.
No sooner ... than
No sooner had we left than the phone rang.
Nada más salir nosotros, sonó el teléfono.
Under no circumstances
Under no circumstances should you open this door.
Bajo ningún concepto debes abrir esta puerta.
Only then / Only when
Only then did I understand.
Solo entonces lo entendí.
Little
Little did she know what was coming.
Poco se imaginaba lo que se le venía encima.

blocks.title: Un orden que el español no tiene
blocks.text: En español basta con poner la palabra delante: Nunca he visto ..., Pocas veces tenemos .... En inglés, después de estas palabras negativas hay que invertir y usar un verbo auxiliar: Never have I seen, Rarely do we get, nunca Never I have seen. Después de palabras normales como yesterday el orden sigue siendo el normal (ver A1 · pdf 8).

head: Con inversión (formal)
Normal
rows: Had I known, I would have come.
If I had known, I would have come.
Were I in your position, I would resign.
If I were in your position, I would resign.
Should you need help, call this number.
If you need help, call this number.

head: Patrón
Ejemplo
Español
rows: It is / was ... that / who
It was Tom who broke the window.
Fue Tom quien rompió la ventana.
What ... is / was
What I need is a holiday.
Lo que necesito son unas vacaciones.
All ... is / was
All I want is some peace.
Lo único que quiero es un poco de paz.
The thing / reason ... is
The reason I'm late is that I missed the bus.
La razón por la que llego tarde es que perdí el autobús.
What happened was
What happened was that the car broke down.
Lo que pasó fue que se averió el coche.

blocks.text: En una frase afirmativa puedes añadir do, does o did para dar énfasis o para llevar la contraria, como el sí que del español: I do like your dress! (¡Sí que me gusta tu vestido!) She did call you; you just didn't hear it. (Sí que te llamó.) Do sit down. (Siéntese, por favor.)

rows: Never I have seen this.
Never have I seen this.
Con never delante: inversión.
Rarely we go out.
Rarely do we go out.
Inversión con do.
Not only it is cheap, but also fast.
Not only is it cheap, but it is also fast.
Después de not only: inversión.
No sooner we had left when it rained.
No sooner had we left than it rained.
No sooner had ... than.
What I need it is a rest.
What I need is a rest.
Sin it de más.
If I would have known, I would have come.
Had I known, I would have come.
Formal, sin if: Had I known.
I do liked it.
I did like it.
Después de did: el verbo sin nada.

blocks.text: Completa con la palabra que falta. Las respuestas están en la última página.

items.full: Never have I heard such nonsense.

items.q: Rarely ______ we see snow in this area.
items.full: Rarely do we see snow in this area.

items.q: Not only ______ she clever, but she is also kind.
items.full: Not only is she clever, but she is also kind.

items.q: No sooner had I sat down ______ the phone rang.
items.full: No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang.

items.q: ______ I known, I would have helped.
items.full: Had I known, I would have helped.

items.q: ______ you have any questions, please contact us.
items.full: Should you have any questions, please contact us.

items.q: ______ I need is a long holiday.
items.full: What I need is a long holiday.

items.q: It was my sister ______ told me the news.
items.full: It was my sister who told me the news.

items.q: Only then ______ I realise my mistake.
items.full: Only then did I realise my mistake.
I do remember locking the door!

items.a: Never have I seen anything like it.

items.q: Fue Tom quien rompió la ventana.
items.a: It was Tom who broke the window.

items.q: De haberlo sabido, habría venido. (formal, sin if)
items.a: Had I known, I would have come.
